title: MicroCT Evaluation of Contrast Agent Infiltration and Diffusion in Synthetic Capillary Models
content: This study explores the infiltration of synthetic capillary channels with radiographically dense materials, with the goal of determining the minimum capillary dimensions that can still be effectively filled. Pulled glass micropipettes serve as molds for fabricating silicone-based microchannels that approximate capillary structures. These channels are then exposed to various radiopaque contrast agents. Pressure-driven flow facilitates material infiltration, with micro-computed tomography (microCT) imaging serving as the primary method for assessing channel filling. In addition, we assess the potential diffusion of these contrast agents into a surrounding solution, as unwanted diffusion could reduce imaging boundary clarity in microCT. By immersing samples in these solutions over time, we evaluate the extent of agent diffusion to determine the stability of the contrast materials within the synthetic channels and shelf stability of samples after contrast enhancement. This analysis provides valuable insight into which agents infiltrate fine capillary structures and maintain well-defined boundaries, thereby improving imaging precision.
